question: Small scale industries in 1950 were defined as all those industries in which the maximum investment was ________ lakh rupees.
solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__ lakh rupees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1950, small scale industries were defined by the maximum investment limit in plant and machinery.
 
• The maximum investment limit for small scale industries was set at **five lakh rupees**.
 
• This definition was intended to encourage the growth and development of small scale industries in India.
 
• The investment limit has been revised multiple times over the years to keep up with inflation and economic changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Small Scale Industries (SSI)**

 
 
• Small Scale Industries are industrial undertakings having a fixed investment in plant and machinery, whether held on an ownership basis or by lease or by hire purchase, not exceeding a prescribed limit.
 
• SSIs play a crucial role in the economic development of a country due to their contribution to employment, production, and exports.
 
• The investment ceiling for SSIs has been revised over the years to reflect changes in economic conditions and industrial growth.
 
• In 1950, the investment limit was set at Rs. 5 lakh, but this limit has been raised periodically to accommodate changes in the economy and inflation.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of SSI Definition**
 
 
• In 1950: The maximum investment limit was Rs. 5 lakh.
 
• In 1966: The investment limit was raised to Rs. 7.5 lakh.
 
• In 1985: The investment limit was further raised to Rs. 35 lakh.
 
• In 1991: The investment limit was raised to Rs. 60 lakh.
 
• In 2006: The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act was enacted, which redefined the criteria for categorizing industries.
 
• As of now, the MSMED Act of 2006 classifies enterprises based on both investment in plant and machinery/equipment and annual turnover.
 
 
 
• **Importance of SSIs**
 
 
• SSIs are vital for economic growth as they provide large-scale employment and contribute significantly to GDP.
 
• They help in the utilization of local resources and promote balanced regional development.
 
• SSIs contribute to the export earnings of the country and help in the development of entrepreneurial skills among the population.
 
• They play a crucial role in the socio-economic development of the country by providing livelihood opportunities.
